evidenceNotes: Standard native rename advertises a boolean provider and returns only WorkspaceEdit. Optional standard progress tokens/unknown extension fields do not require private receipts. Existing strict custom RPC and IDE confirmation/transaction remain compatible. No prepare provider or workspace/applyEdit activation.

The server captures original typed ID, immutable catalog and complete open-document identity/version roster. All project scopes, closed explicit members and open unowned standalone contexts participate. Without workspace-root metadata, a standalone session can use a worker-built empty catalog and existing file contexts. Root/folder sessions without complete configuration fail; folder changes require a fresh full epoch. No implicit directory scan or conversion of open buffers into complete workspace membership.

Reuse existing XRT orchestration/reference workers and actual native source/family/binding/hypothetical checks. Standard export avoids building/discarding private proof DOM and source-body hashes/copies. Both wire formats pass the same final original guard sweep after framing and owner input/epoch/identity/queue gates. Legacy changes map has no versions; applying clients own their transaction and freshness checks.

Fresh native edit oracle covers BOM/CRLF/Unicode, independent raw text edits, version boundaries, legacy-versus-versioned wire equality, all cancellable legacy export positions and7MiB admission. Actual worker framing tests cover typed string ID retention, source disk replacement after encoding, failed framing, cancellation versus physical quiet, detached caller state and no source writes.

Fresh standard stdio matrix includes closed cross-project references, unrelated invalid scope rejection, name conflicts, malformed params, root/file-scope distinctions, explicit configuration refresh, typed concurrent IDs, duplicate IDs, queue capacity and cancellation. This is not complete generic/unbound/foreign qualification.
